title: Fleet op handoff — midweek capacity sketch (2029-06-04)
content:
Midweek handoff sketch — quick captains' notes

Context and intent:
- Purpose: capture what oncall/fleet leads need for the next 48–72h when moving between shifts. Not a full runbook; this is the scratchpad to make the handoff faster and visible.
- Scope: GPU fleet availability, regional preemption patterns, short-term capacity hedges, and one-off experiments that affect routing.

Attendees (sync chat + brief call):
- Avery Chen (owner, fleet ops)
- Kareem Al-Hadi (region lead: APAC)
- Marta Ruiz (sre, EU west)
- Jonah Lee (scheduler/placement)
- Priya Patel (capacity forecasting)

Highlights since last handoff:
- US-West coldstart rate down 18% after rolling the node prewarm patch (PR 472). Average median priming latency dropped from 320ms -> 260ms for baseline generation models on p4d nodes.
- Europe saw an unexpected 3-hr preemption window on 2029-06-03 (0200-0500 UTC) tied to a cluster maintenance batch from cloud provider; cloud ticket OSP-992 flagged, provider acknowledged planned window but not the scale. Impact mitigated via spillover to westeu-burst pool.
- APAC spot volatility spike: 09:45–10:30 JST had a ~24% drop in available accelerators in tokyo-region-2. Backfill succeeded but latency SLOs experienced a 95th percentile spike (~1.2x).

Quick metrics (last 24h rolling) — for shift leads:
- Global spare capacity: ~10% (target 12%); downward trend over 48h (-2pp).
- Reserved committed utilization: 86% average.
- Preemption events: 7 short windows (avg 18 minutes).
- Coldstart tail (99th): 1.1s -> improved in US, unchanged in APAC/EU.
- Cache hit ratio for KV-prefix caching: 68% (goal 75%).

Region notes and actionable items:
- US-West (Avery): keep current prewarm ramp for gen-medium models. Watch pod churn in zone-a-heavy node pool; schedule a diagnostic job to collect kernel OOMs across last 7 days.
  - Action: Jonah to run kernel OOM collector job and post findings by 2029-06-06 EOD.

- Europe (Marta): provider maintenance overlapping with our low-window caused eviction cascade for a handful of canary customers. Suggest adding a canary label to westeu-burst and enforcing a min-available in the autoscaler for that pool.
  - Action: Marta to open autoscaler constraint PR (INFRA-2281) and link the canary list. Due 2029-06-07.

- APAC (Kareem): temporary spike in spot reclaim activity — test earlier prebooking of a small reserved tranche to smooth the morning rush. Forecast suggests this will cost ~3–4% extra but reduce 95th latency by estimated 12%.
  - Action: Priya to add a cost/latency delta to the forecast model and target decision by 2029-06-06 morning.

Experiments and notes to watch:
- Priming warmup fraction tweak (experiment id: priming-2029-06-a): increased warmup fraction from 6% -> 10% for p4d-to-p3 fallback paths. Early signs: improved coldstart tails but increased unit cost by ~1.8%. Watch quality of routing and autoscaler oscillation. Owner: Jonah.
- KV cache TTL adjustment on routing layer: proposed TTL bump for short-lived session prefixes from 30s -> 90s to raise hit ratio. Risk: stale KV usage for multi-turn chat; mitigation: tag sessions created after a model switch to bypass TTL extension. Owner: Avery.

Risks and open questions:
- If provider maintenance windows become more frequent, we need an automated policy to preemptively shift canaries off impacted pools 4–6 hours prior. Is that acceptable for SLA customers? (Product question for later)
- Increased prewarm fraction is improving latency but unit token cost rises — need to formalize a decision rule (cost per p99 improvement) in Optimize. Who owns that rule? (cc: product-optimize)
- Observed node-label churn in apac-edge-1: unclear if this is transient or a scheduler bug. Jonas and platform engineering to pair.

Handoff checklist (what incoming lead should do in first 30 minutes):
1) Check the regional spare capacity dashboards (links in Confluence doc).
2) Confirm no rolling upgrades scheduled in next 6h; if there are, flag to CS.
3) Validate priming experiment health (priming-2029-06-a) — ensure no runaway autoscaler loops.
4) Run quick canary probe (small set of deterministic prompts) against westeu-burst and tokyo-region-2 and record latencies.
5) Tag any incidents with label: fleet-handoff-2029-06-04 and notify SRE rotation.

Action items summary (owner — due):
- Jonah Lee — kernel OOM collector + writeup (2029-06-06).
- Marta Ruiz — autoscaler min-available PR for westeu-burst (INFRA-2281) (2029-06-07).
- Priya Patel — forecast delta for APAC reserved tranche (2029-06-06 morning).
- Avery Chen — deploy KV TTL proposal to staging and run regression prompts (2029-06-05).

Notes / scratch for follow-ups (informal):
- If we accept the APAC reserved tranche, consider tagging it as "opportunistic-reserve" so billing and chargeback are clearer.
- Keep an eye on token-cost telemetry after priming fraction adjustments — correlate with per-route cost buckets.
- We should run a small chaos test in a non-customer lane to validate auto-fallthrough to fallback-models when a region loses ~20% capacity over 10 minutes. Potential ticket: INFRA-2340.

Appendix (links and quick references):
- Priming experiment dashboard (shortlink): https://rdi.redwood/priming/2029-06-a
- Spare capacity heatmap (dash): https://rdi.redwood/dash/spare-heatmap
- Cloud provider support ticket: OSP-992

Quick sign-off: handing to night shift at 2029-06-05 03:15 UTC. If anything looks like >10% changed spare cap, escalate to platform pager and mark: fleet-critical.
